notes: LT-03.4b finite operational retry/overlap/restart scenario oracle. Every scenario is a concrete, finite sequence of request bodies, UUID Idempotency-Key values, actors, instants, logical fault labels and synchronization barriers with exact expected batch/attempt IDs, outcomes, placements and audit phase/action IDs. It reuses the accepted LT-03.4a batches and placements and the LT-03.3b preflight/error payloads wherever a scenario matches them, and declares isolated new batches/selections only where a distinct actor, snapshot or RuleSet is required. No matcher, executor, filesystem writer, recovery engine, concurrency primitive or live restart is implemented: fault points and barriers are logical labels, durable intent phases are declared, and every expected result is a static requirement, not measured evidence. HTTP refusals before a batch use only the error codes the OAS operation declares; per-file results after acceptance are Outcome state/reason pairs.

isolated_batches.reason: Overlap winner: worker1 atomically claims the shared file and moves both its shared and independent safe item; the claim does not change the shared content revision.
Overlap loser: worker2 sees the shared file already claimed, performs no second move for it (SKIPPED/ALREADY_PROCESSING) and still sorts its independent safe item.
A corrected manual retry after the failed preflight uses a new Idempotency-Key and a new selection and therefore produces a new batch and a new attempt.

batch_errors.message: Идемпотентный ключ уже связан с другим телом запроса.
batch_errors.reason: API §2/§8: the same user/operation/key with a different body must be rejected before a second batch is created.

scenarios.title: Lost response then replay after snapshot expiry returns the same DIRECT batch
scenarios.reason: API §2: the existing-key check runs before the dependency-expiry check, so a lost 202 recovers the original durable batch without a second attempt even after the snapshot TTL passed.

fault.setup: Logical: the server durably accepts the batch and returns 202, but the client never observes the response and issues no automatic retry.

scenarios.title: Lost response then replay after preview expiry returns the same PREVIEWED batch
scenarios.reason: API §2: a PREVIEWED batch is recovered with the original key even after the preview TTL passed; the key check precedes STALE_PREVIEW evaluation.

fault.setup: Logical: the durable PREVIEWED acceptance is not observed by the client; no second preview is created.

scenarios.title: Same key with a modified body is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED
scenarios.reason: API §2/§8: the key is bound to the user, operation and body hash; a different body with the same key must not create or return a batch.

scenarios.title: The same key string is a separate scope for another user
scenarios.reason: API §2: the key is bound to user_id, so another user reusing the same string is not IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED and gets that user's own batch.

scenarios.title: A corrected manual retry uses a new key and produces a new attempt
scenarios.reason: QUEUE-09/API §2: a new manual run after an error condition uses a new key; it is not a replay of the failed request and must not reuse the old attempt.

scenarios.title: Two actors overlap on one item plus independent safe items
scenarios.reason: QUEUE-07/API §8: an atomic claim permits at most one real execution; the loser records SKIPPED/ALREADY_PROCESSING with no second move while both independent safe items continue. The claim does not change the content revision.

synchronization.label: synchronized-overlap
synchronization.setup: Logical temporal barrier: the winner claim is committed before the loser attempt, so the loser must observe the active claim.

scenarios.title: A source change is a pre-batch refusal before acceptance and a per-file skip after it
scenarios.reason: API §8: changed sources reject DIRECT (SELECTION_CHANGED) and stale PREVIEWED (STALE_PREVIEW) before any batch or file operation; after durable acceptance the old identity is not moved and the file returns to WAITING_READY.

faults.setup: Logical: the source revision changes after the snapshot/preview and before the batch request; the server rechecks before acceptance.
Logical: the source changes after durable acceptance and before the per-file operation; no operation is performed with the old identity.

scenarios.title: Logout, reload and a new viewer keep the accepted batch and its author
scenarios.reason: AUTH-03/QUEUE-08: an accepted batch keeps running with its original author after logout/reload, is readable by a new viewer, and cannot be cancelled or recreated by that viewer.
scenarios.author: worker1

scenarios.title: A target that appears after acceptance keeps the source and the existing object
scenarios.reason: FILE-01/02/08/API §8: the per-file move is no-replace; a target created after the plan is fixed yields REQUIRES_DECISION/TARGET_OCCUPIED, leaves the source in incoming and never overwrites the existing object.

fault.setup: Logical: an unrelated operation creates the planned target after the plan is fixed and before the per-file move.

scenarios.title: Reversing the input order does not select a duplicate-target winner
scenarios.reason: FILE-03/QUEUE-10: every participant of a shared still-free canonical target gets REQUIRES_DECISION/TARGET_OCCUPIED; processing order never selects a winner and the independent safe file still passes.

scenarios.title: Durable intent across restart before mutation, after proven commit and when ambiguous
scenarios.reason: FILE-09/API §8: intent/phases are persisted before the file action; a proven outcome is recovered without a second move, while an ambiguous placement stays RECOVERY_REQUIRED with no blind retry. These are declared durable-intent requirements, not live restart evidence.

scenarios.title: Containment, foreign scope, invalid path and link replacement use only declared errors
scenarios.reason: FILE-08/API §11: before a batch the server refuses unknown/foreign/invalid targets with the error codes the operation declares; after acceptance a link replacement is a per-file outcome. Every fault is a logical setup, never access outside the synthetic sandbox.

before_batch.fault_setup: Logical: a syntactically valid but unknown selection id is used by an authenticated worker.
Logical: another authenticated user uses a selection bound to a different user_id.
Logical: a display path under the allowed root points at a directory that is not in the configured target list.
Logical: a display path with a prefix other than the allowed sandbox root.
Logical: a malformed relative path with an empty segment.
Logical: an authenticated Atlas worker uses a selection/preview pair that belongs to another company.
Logical: a display path resolves to a configured target of another company.

after_batch.fault_setup: Logical: a link replaces the source between the identity check and the move; the server detects the identity mismatch and performs only a confirmed containment move inside the sandbox.
Logical: a link swap makes the placement ambiguous and no safe containment is proven.

mutations.reason: An idempotent replay must not create an attempt.
A replay returns the original batch.
A modified body with the same key must be 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.
Another user is a separate key scope, not a conflict.
A new manual retry uses a new key.
The losing run must not move the shared file.
A skipped per-file outcome performs no own mutation.
At most one claim/real execution per file.
A claim does not change the content revision.
A source change after acceptance performs no operation.
A changed source returns to WAITING_READY, not READY.
A new viewer never becomes the batch author.
No batch cancel operation exists in the demo contract.
Reversing the input order must not select a winner.
An ambiguous placement must not be retried blindly.
An ambiguous outcome stays RECOVERY_REQUIRED.
A containment fault never permits access outside the sandbox.
createSortingBatch does not declare INVALID_TARGET for 404.
AuditAction is a closed OAS enum.
Unique attempt/phase keys prevent duplicate events.
Only a SYSTEM event may have a null actor; batch acceptance never does.
Every required Q id has at least one scenario.
The Idempotency-Key header is a UUID.
